chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Babawayh, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning a man who has milk with him: may he perform wudu (ablution) with it? He said:

No. It is only water and earth. Thus he negated that anything other than water and earth may be used for purification, by the expression “only,” because that is what is understood from it, as we have explained in the large book.

key_terms.إِنَّمَا: a particle of restriction meaning 'only' or 'nothing but'
key_terms.الصَّعِيدُ: earth or clean ground, the valid medium for tayammum
key_terms.اللَّبَنُ: milk, mentioned here as an invalid substance for purification
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the valid substance for wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Can wudu (ablution) be performed with milk or only with water and earth?
ai.summary: This report states that purification is restricted to water and earth, excluding other substances such as milk from being used for wudu (ablution). The wording emphasizes legal exclusivity, making it a jurisprudential proof concerning ritual purity and tayammum.
